subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (W : Varifold N n U) (X : Euclidean N → Euclidean N) (K : Set (Euclidean N)) (B : ℝ), W.HasLocallyBoundedFirstVariation → ContDiff ℝ 1 X → IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → tsupport X ⊆ K → (∀ z, ‖X z‖ ≤ B) → ENNReal.ofReal |W.firstVariation X| ≤ ENNReal.ofReal B * variationMeasure W K
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon 8.2.5–2.6 (δV(X) = −∫ ν·X d‖δV‖ with |ν| = 1 ‖δV‖-a.e.), the estimate used in step 3 of the parent proof to bound |δW(X_t)|. Notation: ‖δW‖ := variationMeasure W; hW the locally-bounded-first-variation hypothesis.

1. X is a test field of U: it is C¹; tsupport X ⊆ K with K compact, so tsupport X is a closed subset of a compact set, hence compact, i.e. HasCompactSupport X; and tsupport X ⊆ K ⊆ U. Let T : Varifold.TestVectorField U be the test field with underlying function X.

2. Since hW holds, variationMeasure W = W.firstVariationRieszMeasure hW =: λ (definition of variationMeasure, positive branch of the dependent if). By Varifold.isFirstVariationPolarRepresentation_riesz, with ν := W.firstVariationPolarField hW: ‖ν(x)‖ = 1 for λ-a.e. x, and for the test field T the function x ↦ ⟨ν(x), X(x)⟩ is λ-integrable with W.firstVariation X = −∫⟨ν(x), X(x)⟩ dλ(x).

3. Hence ofReal|W.firstVariation X| = ‖∫⟨ν, X⟩ dλ‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻ ‖⟨ν(x), X(x)⟩‖ₑ dλ(x) (Real.enorm_eq_ofReal_abs, enorm_integral_le_lintegral_enorm).

4. For λ-a.e. x: if x ∈ K, then ‖⟨ν(x), X(x)⟩‖ ≤ ‖ν(x)‖·‖X(x)‖ = ‖X(x)‖ ≤ B (norm_inner_le_norm), so ‖⟨ν(x), X(x)⟩‖ₑ ≤ ofReal B = 1_K(x)·ofReal B; if x ∉ K, then x ∉ tsupport X, so X(x) = 0 and the integrand is 0 = 1_K(x)·ofReal B.

5. Therefore ∫⁻ ‖⟨ν, X⟩‖ₑ dλ ≤ ∫⁻ 1_K·ofReal B dλ = ofReal B·λ(K) (lintegral_mono_ae; lintegral_indicator_const, K being closed hence Borel). With step 3: ofReal|W.firstVariation X| ≤ ofReal B · variationMeasure W K. ∎
proof_key_steps: X is a TestVectorField of U (C¹, compact support inside K ⊆ U)
variationMeasure W is the Riesz measure; polar representation δW(X) = −∫⟨ν,X⟩ d‖δW‖ with |ν| = 1 a.e.
ofReal|δW(X)| ≤ ∫⁻ ‖⟨ν,X⟩‖ₑ d‖δW‖
Pointwise a.e.: ‖⟨ν,X⟩‖ₑ ≤ 1_K·ofReal B (X = 0 off tsupport X ⊆ K)
Integrate: ≤ ofReal B·‖δW‖(K)

subproblems.title: Tangential divergence of a radial-type field: div_S(a(·)(· − y)) = n·a + Da[p_S(z − y)]
subproblems.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, a : ℝ^N → ℝ differentiable at z ∈ ℝ^N, y ∈ ℝ^N and S ∈ G(N,n). Then the tangential divergence (Varifold.tangentialDivergence, the trace of S.1 times the Jacobian matrix) of the field w ↦ a(w)(w − y) at z with respect to S equals n·a(z) + Da(z)[p_S(z − y)], where p_S = Grassmannian.project S.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (a : Euclidean N → ℝ) (y z : Euclidean N) (S : Grassmannian N n), DifferentiableAt ℝ a z → Varifold.tangentialDivergence (fun w ↦ a w • (w - y)) z S = n * a z + fderiv ℝ a z (Grassmannian.project S (z - y))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the pointwise computation underlying Simon 8.3.3 and 8.3.5 (the tangential divergence of the radial fields used there), needed in step 3 of the parent proof for X_t(z) = h(z)φ(|z − y|²/t²)(z − y). Notation: p_S := Grassmannian.project S = projectionLinearMap S, a linear map whose matrix in the standard orthonormal basis is S.1; Y(w) := a(w)(w − y).

1. The map w ↦ w − y is differentiable with derivative the identity. By the product rule (fderiv_fun_smul), Y is differentiable at z with DY(z) = a(z)·id + Da(z).smulRight(z − y), i.e. DY(z)[v] = a(z)v + Da(z)[v]·(z − y).

2. By definition, div_S Y(z) = Matrix.trace(S.1 · jacobian Y z), and jacobian Y z is the matrix of DY(z) in the standard basis (Varifold.jacobian_eq_toMatrix). Since S.1 is the matrix of p_S in the same basis, LinearMap.trace_eq_matrix_trace and LinearMap.toMatrix_comp give div_S Y(z) = LinearMap.trace(p_S ∘ DY(z)).

3. Composition: p_S ∘ DY(z) = a(z)·p_S + Da(z).smulRight(p_S(z − y)), since p_S(a(z)v + Da(z)[v](z − y)) = a(z)p_S v + Da(z)[v]·p_S(z − y) for every v.

4. The trace of p_S equals the trace of its matrix S.1, which is n (Grassmannian.trace_eq); and the trace of the rank-one map v ↦ ℓ(v)u equals ℓ(u) (LinearMap.trace_smulRight). By linearity of the trace,
 div_S Y(z) = a(z)·n + Da(z)[p_S(z − y)] = n·a(z) + Da(z)[Grassmannian.project S (z − y)]. ∎
proof_key_steps: Product rule: DY(z) = a(z)·id + Da(z).smulRight(z − y)
div_S Y(z) = trace(S.1·jacobian) = LinearMap.trace(p_S ∘ DY(z))
p_S ∘ DY(z) = a(z)p_S + Da(z).smulRight(p_S(z − y))
trace p_S = n and trace(ℓ.smulRight u) = ℓ(u) give n·a(z) + Da(z)[p_S(z − y)]

subproblems.title: Weighted radial monotonicity with error terms for a fixed cutoff (Simon 8.3.5 integrated over [σ, ρ])
subproblems.statement: Let W be an n-varifold on U ⊆ ℝ^N with locally bounded first variation, P ∈ G(N,n), y ∈ ℝ^N with B°_1(y) ⊆ U, ε > 0, K ≥ 0, M ≥ 0, and assume for every r ∈ (0,1): (1r) ‖δW‖(B_r(y)) ≤ εμ_W(B_r(y)); (2r) ∫_{B_r(y)×G(N,n)} t_P(S) dW(z,S) ≤ εr^n (t_P(S) = operator norm of p_S − p_P); (3r) μ_W(B_r(y)) ≤ Kr^n. Let h : ℝ^N → [0,1] be C¹ with |Dh(z)[p_S(z − y)]| ≤ M·t_P(S)·|z − y| for all z ∈ ℝ^N and S ∈ G(N,n), and let φ : ℝ → [0,1] be C¹ and non-increasing with φ(s) = 0 for s ≥ A², where 0 < A ≤ 2. Then for all 0 < σ ≤ ρ with ρA < 1, writing Ĩ(t) := ∫ φ(|z − y|²/t²)h(z) dμ_W(z) (Bochner integral): Ĩ(σ)/σ^n ≤ Ĩ(ρ)/ρ^n + 2^{n+1}(M + K)ερ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (W : Varifold N n U) (P : Grassmannian N n) (y : Euclidean N) (ε K M A : ℝ) (h : Euclidean N → ℝ) (φ : ℝ → ℝ), W.HasLocallyBoundedFirstVariation → ball y 1 ⊆ U → 0 < ε → 0 ≤ K → 0 ≤ M → (∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → r < 1 → variationMeasure W (closedBall y r) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal ε * W.weight (closedBall y r)) → (∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → r < 1 → (∫⁻ z in closedBall y r ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n)), ENNReal.ofReal ‖LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap (Grassmannian.projectionLinearMap z.2 - Grassmannian.projectionLinearMap P)‖ ∂W.measure) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (ε * r ^ n)) → (∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → r < 1 → W.weight (closedBall y r) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (K * r ^ n)) → ContDiff ℝ 1 h → (∀ z, 0 ≤ h z ∧ h z ≤ 1) → (∀ (z : Euclidean N) (S : Grassmannian N n), |fderiv ℝ h z (Grassmannian.project S (z - y))| ≤ M * ‖LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap (Grassmannian.projectionLinearMap S - Grassmannian.projectionLinearMap P)‖ * ‖z - y‖) → ContDiff ℝ 1 φ → Antitone φ → (∀ s, 0 ≤ φ s ∧ φ s ≤ 1) → 0 < A → A ≤ 2 → (∀ s, A ^ 2 ≤ s → φ s = 0) → ∀ σ ρ : ℝ, 0 < σ → σ ≤ ρ → ρ * A < 1 → (∫ z, φ (‖z - y‖ ^ 2 / σ ^ 2) * h z ∂W.weight) / σ ^ n ≤ (∫ z, φ (‖z - y‖ ^ 2 / ρ ^ 2) * h z ∂W.weight) / ρ ^ n + 2 ^ (n + 1) * (M + K) * ε * ρ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon 8.3.5 (the weighted monotonicity identity), integrated over [σ, ρ] and combined with the error estimates of step 3 of the parent proof (Simon 8.5.10, printed (7)). ERRATUM (E2): the coefficient of δV(X) in 3.5 is '−' (SimonGMT Chapter08/WeightedRadialIdentity.lean). SimonGMT's Varifold.hasDerivAt_normalized_weightedCutoffMass is outside Submission's import closure, so the needed inequality is derived here from the definitions.
Notation. μ := W.weight; ‖δW‖ := variationMeasure W; B_r(y) := closedBall y r; G := Grassmannian N n. For S ∈ G, p_S := Grassmannian.project S, a self-adjoint idempotent linear map, so ⟨v, p_S v⟩ = ‖p_S v‖² ≤ ‖v‖². t_P(S) := ‖LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap(projectionLinearMap S − projectionLinearMap P)‖. For z ∈ ℝ^N, w := z − y.

1. Preliminaries on φ. φ' is continuous, so it is bounded on the compact interval [0, A²]; let L_φ be such a bound. Only arguments s = ‖w‖²/t² ≥ 0 occur, and φ' = 0 on (A², ∞). Since φ is non-increasing and differentiable, φ' ≤ 0 everywhere: difference quotients of a non-increasing function are ≤ 0.

2. Radius. Put R := (ρA + 1)/2, so ρA < R < 1. Then closedBall y R ⊆ ball y 1 ⊆ U, and μ(B_R(y)) = W.measure(B_R(y) ×ˢ univ) < ∞, because W is finite on compact subsets of U (Varifold.weight_finite_on_compact).

3. Test fields. For t > 0 let a_t(z) := h(z)φ(‖w‖²/t²) and X_t(z) := a_t(z)(z − y).
 a_t is C¹, with Da_t(z)[v] = φ(‖w‖²/t²)Dh(z)[v] + h(z)φ'(‖w‖²/t²)(2/t²)⟨w, v⟩; so X_t is C¹.
 If ‖w‖ ≥ tA then ‖w‖²/t² ≥ A², so φ(‖w‖²/t²) = 0 and X_t(z) = 0. Hence tsupport X_t ⊆ closedBall y (tA), and ‖X_t(z)‖ ≤ tA for all z (0 ≤ h, φ ≤ 1).
 By the sibling radial_field_divergence (applied to a_t, which is differentiable) and ⟨w, p_S w⟩ = ‖p_S w‖², for all z and S:
  (D) div_S X_t(z) = n·a_t(z) + φ(‖w‖²/t²)·Dh(z)[p_S w] + (2/t²)h(z)φ'(‖w‖²/t²)‖p_S w‖².

4. Integrals. For t ∈ (0, R/A) define
  Ĩ(t) := ∫ φ(‖w‖²/t²)h(z) dμ(z),  J(t) := ∫ (2‖w‖²/t³)(−φ'(‖w‖²/t²))h(z) dμ(z),
  G(t) := ∫ φ(‖w‖²/t²)·Dh(z)[p_S w] dW(z,S),  Q(t) := ∫ (2/t²)h(z)(−φ'(‖w‖²/t²))(‖w‖² − ‖p_S w‖²) dW(z,S).
 Each integrand is measurable and bounded (the derivatives involved are continuous), and vanishes unless ‖w‖ < tA < R. So each is integrable against the finite measure μ restricted to B_R(y), respectively W.measure restricted to B_R(y) ×ˢ univ. Moreover J(t) ≥ 0 and Q(t) ≥ 0, because φ' ≤ 0, h ≥ 0 and ‖p_S w‖ ≤ ‖w‖. Since μ = (Prod.fst)_# W.measure, the integral of a function of z against μ equals the integral of the same function of z.1 against W.measure (integral_map).

5. Derivative of Ĩ. Let t₀ ∈ (0, R/A); we show Ĩ has derivative J(t₀) at t₀.
 F(t,z) := φ(‖w‖²/t²)h(z) is differentiable in t > 0, with ∂_tF(t,z) = (−2‖w‖²/t³)φ'(‖w‖²/t²)h(z).
 Put t₁ := (t₀ + R/A)/2. For t ∈ (t₀/2, t₁), ∂_tF(t,·) vanishes outside B_R(y) and is bounded by L_φ·2(t₁A)²/(t₀/2)³. That constant on B_R(y) is a μ-integrable bound.
 So differentiation under the integral sign (hasDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_loc_of_deriv_le) gives Ĩ'(t₀) = J(t₀).

6. Weighted radial inequality. By definition W.firstVariation X_t = ∫ div_S X_t(z) dW(z,S). Integrating (D), whose three terms are integrable:
  δW(X_t) = n·Ĩ(t) + G(t) − ∫ (2/t²)h(−φ'(‖w‖²/t²))‖p_S w‖² dW.
 Also t·J(t) = ∫ (2/t²)h(−φ'(‖w‖²/t²))‖w‖² dW. Subtracting,
  t·Ĩ'(t) − n·Ĩ(t) = t·J(t) − n·Ĩ(t) = G(t) − δW(X_t) + Q(t) ≥ G(t) − δW(X_t).
 Hence t ↦ Ĩ(t)/t^n is differentiable on (0, R/A), with derivative (t·Ĩ'(t) − n·Ĩ(t))/t^{n+1} ≥ (G(t) − δW(X_t))/t^{n+1}.

7. Error bounds for t ∈ [σ, ρ]. Here 0 < tA ≤ ρA < 1 and t < R/A.
 (a) Apply the sibling first_variation_bound to X_t with K' := closedBall y (tA), which is compact and ⊆ U, and bound tA: |δW(X_t)| ≤ tA·‖δW‖(B_{tA}(y)). By (1r) and (3r) at radius tA ∈ (0,1), ‖δW‖(B_{tA}(y)) ≤ ε·μ(B_{tA}(y)) ≤ εK(tA)^n. So |δW(X_t)| ≤ A^{n+1}Kε·t^{n+1}.
 (b) The integrand of G vanishes unless ‖w‖ < tA. There, by the gradient hypothesis and 0 ≤ φ ≤ 1, its absolute value is ≤ M·t_P(S)·tA. So, using (2r) at radius tA,
  |G(t)| ≤ M·tA·∫_{B_{tA}(y)×G} t_P dW ≤ M·tA·ε(tA)^n = M·A^{n+1}ε·t^{n+1}.
 (c) Therefore, by step 6, d/dt(Ĩ(t)/t^n) ≥ −A^{n+1}(M + K)ε ≥ −2^{n+1}(M + K)ε on [σ, ρ], since 0 < A ≤ 2.

8. Integration. F(t) := Ĩ(t)/t^n + 2^{n+1}(M + K)ε·t is differentiable at every point of [σ, ρ] with F' ≥ 0 there. So it is non-decreasing on [σ, ρ] (monotoneOn_of_deriv_nonneg on the convex set [σ, ρ]), and
  Ĩ(σ)/σ^n ≤ Ĩ(ρ)/ρ^n + 2^{n+1}(M + K)ε(ρ − σ) ≤ Ĩ(ρ)/ρ^n + 2^{n+1}(M + K)ερ. ∎
proof_key_steps: φ' ≤ 0 and φ' bounded on [0, A²]; R := (ρA + 1)/2 gives closedBall y R ⊆ U with finite mass
X_t = h·φ(‖·−y‖²/t²)·(· − y) is C¹, supported in closedBall y (tA), |X_t| ≤ tA; divergence (D) via radial_field_divergence
Ĩ'(t) = J(t) by differentiation under the integral sign
Integrating (D): tĨ' − nĨ = G − δW(X_t) + Q ≥ G − δW(X_t)
|δW(X_t)| ≤ A^{n+1}Kεt^{n+1} (first_variation_bound with (1r), (3r)); |G| ≤ MA^{n+1}εt^{n+1} (gradient hypothesis, (2r))
d/dt(Ĩ/t^n) ≥ −2^{n+1}(M+K)ε; monotonicity of Ĩ(t)/t^n + 2^{n+1}(M+K)εt on [σ,ρ]

subproblems.title: Cylinder monotonicity at good points (Simon 8.5.10, printed (7))
subproblems.statement: For all N, n ∈ ℕ there is C ≥ 0 such that: let W be an n-varifold on U ⊆ ℝ^N with locally bounded first variation, P ∈ G(N,n), y ∈ ℝ^N with B°_1(y) ⊆ U, ε > 0, K ≥ 0, and assume for every r ∈ (0,1): (1r) ‖δW‖(B_r(y)) ≤ ε μ_W(B_r(y)); (2r) ∫_{B_r(y)×G(N,n)} t_P(S) dW(z,S) ≤ ε r^n (t_P(S) = operator norm of p_S − p_P); (3r) μ_W(B_r(y)) ≤ K r^n. Then for all 0 < τ ≤ 1 and 0 < σ ≤ ρ < 1, with U^τ_σ(y) := B_σ(y) ∩ {z : |(z − y) − p_P(z − y)| < τ}: μ_W(U^τ_σ(y))/σ^n ≤ μ_W(U^{2τ}_ρ(y))/ρ^n + C(1 + K)ερ/τ in [0,∞].
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ), ∃ C : ℝ, 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (W : Varifold N n U) (P : Grassmannian N n) (y : Euclidean N) (ε K : ℝ), W.HasLocallyBoundedFirstVariation → ball y 1 ⊆ U → 0 < ε → 0 ≤ K → (∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → r < 1 → variationMeasure W (closedBall y r) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal ε * W.weight (closedBall y r)) → (∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → r < 1 → (∫⁻ z in closedBall y r ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n)), ENNReal.ofReal ‖LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap (Grassmannian.projectionLinearMap z.2 - Grassmannian.projectionLinearMap P)‖ ∂W.measure) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (ε * r ^ n)) → (∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → r < 1 → W.weight (closedBall y r) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (K * r ^ n)) → ∀ τ σ ρ : ℝ, 0 < τ → τ ≤ 1 → 0 < σ → σ ≤ ρ → ρ < 1 → W.weight (closedBall y σ ∩ {z | ‖(z - y) - Grassmannian.project P (z - y)‖ < τ}) / ENNReal.ofReal σ ^ n ≤ W.weight (closedBall y ρ ∩ {z | ‖(z - y) - Grassmannian.project P (z - y)‖ < 2 * τ}) / ENNReal.ofReal ρ ^ n + ENNReal.ofReal (C * (1 + K) * ε * ρ / τ)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent proof (Simon 8.5.10, printed (7), 'proved by simply integrating 3.5'). The parent's constant c3 = 2^{n+1}(4 + c1ω_n) is replaced by C(1 + K) with C := 2^{n+1}(4L + 1), where L bounds |Real.smoothTransition'|; no numerical value of L is needed. The integrated identity 3.5 with its error terms is the sibling weighted_radial_monotonicity.
Notation. μ := W.weight; B_r(y) := closedBall y r, B°_r(y) := ball y r; G := Grassmannian N n.
 p := Grassmannian.project P, the linear map projectionLinearMap P, self-adjoint (projectionLinearMap_isSymmetric) and idempotent (project_project).
 q(v) := v − p(v). It is linear, self-adjoint and idempotent, with p(q v) = 0 and ‖v‖² = ‖p v‖² + ‖q v‖², so ‖q v‖ ≤ ‖v‖.
 For S ∈ G, p_S := Grassmannian.project S (self-adjoint). t_P(S) := ‖LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap(projectionLinearMap S − projectionLinearMap P)‖, so ‖p_S v − p v‖ ≤ t_P(S)‖v‖ (ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm).
 U^τ_σ(y) := B_σ(y) ∩ {z : ‖q(z − y)‖ < τ}, closed ∩ open, hence Borel.
 st := Real.smoothTransition: C^∞, monotone, values in [0,1], st = 0 on (−∞,0], st = 1 on [1,∞).

0. The constant. Fix L ≥ 0 with |st'(u)| ≤ L for all u ∈ ℝ. Such an L exists: st' is continuous, hence bounded on [−1,2], and st' = 0 outside [0,1], where st is locally constant. Put C := 2^{n+1}(4L + 1) ≥ 0; it depends only on n.
 Fix U, W, P, y, ε, K satisfying the hypotheses, τ ∈ (0,1] and 0 < σ ≤ ρ < 1.

1. Radial cutoffs. Fix η₀ ∈ (0,1] with (1 + η₀)ρ < 1 (e.g. η₀ := min{1, (1 − ρ)/(2ρ)}). For η ∈ (0,η₀] let A_η := 1 + η ∈ (0,2] and φ_η(s) := st((A_η² − s)/(A_η² − 1)). Then:
 – φ_η is C^∞ (hence C¹) and non-increasing (Antitone);
 – 0 ≤ φ_η ≤ 1;
 – φ_η(s) = 1 for s ≤ 1 and φ_η(s) = 0 for s ≥ A_η²;
 – ρA_η ≤ ρ(1 + η₀) < 1.

2. The weight h. Let g(s) := st(4 − s) and h(z) := g(‖q(z − y)‖²/τ²).
 (a) g is C^∞ and non-increasing, 0 ≤ g ≤ 1, g = 1 on (−∞,3], g = 0 on [4,∞), |g'| ≤ L, and g'(s) = 0 unless 3 < s < 4.
 (b) h is C^∞, being a composition of the continuous affine map z ↦ q(z − y), the C^∞ map v ↦ ‖v‖² (contDiff_norm_sq), division by τ², and g. Also 0 ≤ h ≤ 1.
 (c) h(z) = 1 if ‖q(z − y)‖ < τ, and h(z) = 0 if ‖q(z − y)‖ ≥ 2τ. Hence, pointwise, 1_{U^τ_σ(y)} ≤ 1_{B_σ(y)}·h and 1_{B_ρ(y)}·h ≤ 1_{U^{2τ}_ρ(y)}.
 (d) Gradient bound. Let z, v ∈ ℝ^N and w := z − y. The chain rule gives
  Dh(z)[v] = g'(‖q w‖²/τ²)·(2/τ²)⟨q w, q v⟩ = g'(‖q w‖²/τ²)·(2/τ²)⟨q w, v⟩.
 For S ∈ G, self-adjointness of p_S and p(q w) = 0 give ⟨q w, p_S w⟩ = ⟨p_S(q w), w⟩ = ⟨(p_S − p)(q w), w⟩, so |⟨q w, p_S w⟩| ≤ t_P(S)‖q w‖‖w‖. Moreover g'(‖q w‖²/τ²) ≠ 0 forces ‖q w‖ < 2τ. Hence for all z and S:
  (G) |Dh(z)[p_S(z − y)]| ≤ (4L/τ)·t_P(S)·‖z − y‖.

3. Fixed cutoff. For η ∈ (0,η₀] apply the sibling weighted_radial_monotonicity with h, φ := φ_η, A := A_η and M := 4L/τ ≥ 0. Its hypotheses are (1r), (2r), (3r), (G), step 1, step 2(b) and ρA_η < 1. Writing Ĩ_η(t) := ∫ φ_η(‖z − y‖²/t²)h(z) dμ(z), it gives
  Ĩ_η(σ)/σ^n ≤ Ĩ_η(ρ)/ρ^n + 2^{n+1}(4L/τ + K)ερ.

4. Limit η ↓ 0. Take η_j := η₀/(j + 1). Fix t ∈ {σ, ρ} and z.
 – If ‖z − y‖ ≤ t, then φ_{η_j}(‖z − y‖²/t²) = 1 for all j.
 – If ‖z − y‖ > t, then A_{η_j}² ≤ ‖z − y‖²/t² for all large j, so φ_{η_j}(…) = 0 eventually.
 Thus φ_{η_j}(‖z − y‖²/t²)h(z) → 1_{B_t(y)}(z)h(z) pointwise. The dominating function 1_{B_{t(1+η₀)}(y)} is μ-integrable, since closedBall y (t(1+η₀)) is a compact subset of U. By dominated convergence (tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence), Ĩ_{η_j}(t) → I(t) := ∫_{B_t(y)} h dμ. Step 3 passes to the limit:

subproblems.title: Cluster selection for a finite fibre (Simon 8.5.10, proof of (8), step 5(c))
subproblems.statement: Let N ∈ ℕ, s ⊆ ℝ^N a finite set with k := #s ≥ 2, and d > 0 such that |y − y'| ≥ d for all distinct y, y' ∈ s and |y₀ − y₁| ≤ d for some distinct y₀, y₁ ∈ s. Then there are Z ⊆ s and S ≥ 0 with #Z < #s, S ≤ (10k)^k d, every y ∈ s within distance S of some z ∈ Z, and |z − z'| ≥ 2d + 4S for all distinct z, z' ∈ Z.

Source: step 5(c) of the parent proof (Simon 8.5.10, proof of (8): 'we can select {z_1,…,z_Q} ⊆ {y_1,…,y_N} (Q ≤ N − 1) and τ̂ ≥ τ̃ … such that τ̂ ≤ ¼ min_{i≠j}|z_i − z_j|'). The book gives no construction. The parent's construction, via connected components of distance graphs, is replaced here by an equivalent greedy merging argument with the same conclusion, because Mathlib's SimpleGraph connectivity is outside Submission's import closure. Let k := #s ≥ 2.

1. Call a pair (Z, S) admissible if Z ⊆ s, Z ≠ ∅, #Z < k, S ≥ 0, every y ∈ s has some z ∈ Z with ‖y − z‖ ≤ S, and S ≤ d(5^{k − #Z} − 1)/2.

2. An admissible pair exists. Let y₀ ≠ y₁ in s with ‖y₀ − y₁‖ ≤ d, and put Z₁ := s \ {y₁}, S₁ := d. Then Z₁ ⊆ s, y₀ ∈ Z₁, #Z₁ = k − 1 < k and S₁ ≥ 0. Every y ∈ s other than y₁ lies in Z₁ (distance 0 ≤ d), and ‖y₁ − y₀‖ ≤ d. Finally d ≤ d(5¹ − 1)/2 = 2d.

3. Among the admissible pairs choose (Z, S) with #Z minimal. The cardinalities of admissible pairs form a nonempty set of natural numbers (Nat.find or a well-founded minimum).

4. Separation. Suppose distinct z, z' ∈ Z satisfy ‖z − z'‖ < 2d + 4S. Put Z' := Z \ {z'} and S' := 2d + 5S. Then Z' ⊆ s, z ∈ Z' (so Z' ≠ ∅), #Z' = #Z − 1 < k, and S' ≥ 0.
 Covering: for y ∈ s pick z'' ∈ Z with ‖y − z''‖ ≤ S. If z'' ≠ z', then z'' ∈ Z' and ‖y − z''‖ ≤ S ≤ S'. If z'' = z', then ‖y − z‖ ≤ ‖y − z'‖ + ‖z' − z‖ < S + 2d + 4S = S'.
 Bound: S' = 2d + 5S ≤ 2d + 5d(5^{k−#Z} − 1)/2 = d(5^{k−#Z+1} − 1)/2 = d(5^{k−#Z'} − 1)/2.
 So (Z', S') is admissible with #Z' < #Z, contradicting minimality. Hence ‖z − z'‖ ≥ 2d + 4S for all distinct z, z' ∈ Z.

5. Conclusion. The pair (Z, S) of step 3 satisfies Z ⊆ s, #Z < #s, 0 ≤ S, the covering property, and (step 4) the separation property. Since #Z ≥ 1, S ≤ d(5^{k−1} − 1)/2 ≤ 5^k d ≤ (10k)^k d (5 ≤ 10k, d > 0). ∎

Take an admissible pair with #Z minimal
If two centres were closer than 2d + 4S, deleting one and setting S' = 2d + 5S gives a smaller admissible pair — contradiction
Hence separation ‖z − z'‖ ≥ 2d + 4S, and S ≤ 5^k d ≤ (10k)^k d

Source: step 5 of the parent proof (Simon 8.5.10, printed (8), proved by induction on the number of points). Here it is in abstract form: μ is any Borel measure on ℝ^N, and the only properties of the points used are p(y) = x, ‖y − p(y)‖ < ε, (M_y) and (C_y). (C_y) is the parent's step 3 with its constant written as K, without the factor 1/ω_n. The parent's cases m = 1 and m ≥ 2 are unified. The bound is claimed for all σ ≤ δ², which for one point implies σ ≤ 1 − ε. The condition τ ≤ d/4 is written as 4τ ≤ ‖y − y'‖ for distinct y, y' ∈ s, which is vacuous for one point.
Notation. p := Grassmannian.project P; q(v) := v − p(v) (linear, ‖q v‖ ≤ ‖v‖, and q(v) = v when p(v) = 0); B_r(y) := closedBall y r; U^τ_σ(y) := B_σ(y) ∩ {z : ‖q(z − y)‖ < τ} (Borel). Inequalities between measures are in [0,∞], and real coefficients enter through ENNReal.ofReal.

0. Elementary facts, for δ ∈ (0,1/2] and ε ∈ (0,δ⁴]: ε ≤ δ⁴ ≤ δ² ≤ 1/4 and ε ≤ 1/16.
 (F1) (1 + u)^n ≤ 1 + (2^n − 1)u for u ∈ [0,1], since (1 + u)^n − 1 = u·Σ_{j<n}(1 + u)^j ≤ u·Σ_{j<n}2^j.
 (F2) e^ε ≤ 1 + 2ε and (1 − ε)^{−1} ≤ 1 + 2ε for ε ∈ [0,1/2].
 (F3) U^τ_σ(y) ⊆ U^{τ'}_{σ'}(y) for τ ≤ τ', σ ≤ σ'; and U^τ_σ(y) ⊆ B_σ(y).
 (F4) If p(y) = p(y') = x, then y − x = q(y) and y − y' = q(y − y').

1. One point. Let δ ∈ (0,1/2], ε ∈ (0,δ⁴], s = {y} with the hypotheses, 0 < σ ≤ δ² and τ > 0. Then σ ≤ 1/4 < 1 − ε < 1. By (F3), e^{εσ} ≥ 1 and (M_y) applied to σ ≤ 1 − ε:
 μ(U^τ_σ(y))/σ^n ≤ μ(B_σ(y))/σ^n ≤ e^{εσ}μ(B_σ(y))/σ^n ≤ e^{ε(1−ε)}μ(B_{1−ε}(y))/(1−ε)^n ≤ e^ε(1−ε)^{−n}μ(B_1(x)).
 The last step uses B_{1−ε}(y) ⊆ B_1(x), since ‖z − x‖ ≤ ‖z − y‖ + ‖y − x‖ < (1 − ε) + ε.
 By (F1)–(F2) with u = 2ε ≤ 1: e^ε(1−ε)^{−n} ≤ (1 + 2ε)(1 + (2^n − 1)2ε) ≤ 1 + 2^{n+1}ε + 2^{n+2}ε² ≤ 1 + 2^{n+2}ε ≤ 1 + 2^{n+2}δ².
 So the claimed bound holds whenever c ≥ 2^{n+2}. If s = ∅ the sum is 0.

2. Constants, by recursion on m. Set c_0 := 0, δ_0 := 1/2. Given c_m ≥ 0 and δ_m > 0, put a := 4(10(m+1))^{m+1} ≥ 1, b := (2^n − 1)a, and
 c_{m+1} := max{2^{n+2}, b + c_m + b·c_m, (1 + b)c_m + (m+1)K},  δ_{m+1} := min{δ_m, 1/a}.
 Then c_{m+1} ≥ 0 and 0 < δ_{m+1} ≤ 1/a ≤ 1/40 ≤ 1/2, because a ≥ 40. So δ ≤ 1/2 holds automatically for δ ≤ δ_{m+1}, and the frozen ∃-statement can be proved by plain induction on m without strengthening the motive. Also aδ² ≤ 1 for 0 < δ ≤ δ_{m+1}, since a ≥ 1.

3. Induction. The claim for m = 0 is trivial (s = ∅). Assume it for m with constants (c_m, δ_m); we prove it for m + 1 with (c_{m+1}, δ_{m+1}).
 Let δ ∈ (0,δ_{m+1}], ε ∈ (0,δ⁴], and μ, P, x, s with #s ≤ m + 1 and the per-point hypotheses. Let σ, τ satisfy 0 < σ ≤ δ², 2δ²σ ≤ τ, and 4τ ≤ ‖y − y'‖ for distinct y, y' ∈ s.
 If #s ≤ 1, step 1 applies, since c_{m+1} ≥ 2^{n+2}. So let k := #s ≥ 2 and d := min{‖y − y'‖ : y, y' ∈ s, y ≠ y'}, attained at some pair. By (F4), ‖y − y'‖ ≤ ‖y − x‖ + ‖y' − x‖ < 2ε, so 0 < d < 2ε ≤ 1/8; and 4τ ≤ d.

4. Scales. ρ := d/(4δ²) and τ̃ := d/2 = 2δ²ρ. Then σ ≤ τ/(2δ²) ≤ d/(8δ²) < ρ, and ρ < 2ε/(4δ²) ≤ δ²/2 < 1.

5. (a) First comparison. For y ∈ s we have τ ≤ d/4. By (F3) and (C_y) with parameter d/4 ∈ (0,1] and radii σ ≤ ρ < 1:
 μ(U^τ_σ(y))/σ^n ≤ μ(U^{d/4}_σ(y))/σ^n ≤ μ(U^{τ̃}_ρ(y))/ρ^n + Kερ/(d/4) = μ(U^{τ̃}_ρ(y))/ρ^n + Kε/δ² ≤ μ(U^{τ̃}_ρ(y))/ρ^n + Kδ².
 The set produced by (C_y), {z : ‖q(z − y)‖ < 2·(d/4)}, equals {z : ‖q(z − y)‖ < d/2} = the τ̃-cylinder condition (rewrite 2·(d/4) = d/2 inside the set-builder).
 Summing over the k ≤ m + 1 points: Σ_{y∈s} μ(U^τ_σ(y))/σ^n ≤ Σ_{y∈s} μ(U^{τ̃}_ρ(y))/ρ^n + (m+1)Kδ².

6. (b) Disjointness. For distinct y, y' ∈ s, U^{τ̃}_ρ(y) ∩ U^{τ̃}_ρ(y') = ∅. A common point z would give, by (F4) and linearity of q,
 ‖y − y'‖ = ‖q(y − y')‖ = ‖q(z − y') − q(z − y)‖ ≤ ‖q(z − y)‖ + ‖q(z − y')‖ < 2τ̃ = d,
 contradicting the definition of d.

7. (c) Clusters. Apply the sibling cluster_selection to s and d: #s ≥ 2, d > 0, d ≤ ‖y − y'‖ for distinct points, and equality is attained. It gives Z ⊆ s and S ≥ 0 with #Z < k, S ≤ (10k)^k d ≤ (10(m+1))^{m+1}d, every y ∈ s within S of some r(y) ∈ Z (choose such an r(y)), and ‖z − z'‖ ≥ 2d + 4S for distinct z, z' ∈ Z. Put τ̂ := τ̃ + S and ρ̂ := ρ + S. Then:
 – U^{τ̃}_ρ(y) ⊆ U^{τ̂}_{ρ̂}(r(y)) for y ∈ s. For z in the left side, ‖z − r(y)‖ ≤ ‖z − y‖ + ‖y − r(y)‖ ≤ ρ + S, and ‖q(z − r(y))‖ ≤ ‖q(z − y)‖ + ‖q(y − r(y))‖ < τ̃ + ‖y − r(y)‖ ≤ τ̂.
 – S ≤ (10(m+1))^{m+1}·4δ²ρ = aδ²ρ (as d = 4δ²ρ), so ρ ≤ ρ̂ ≤ ρ(1 + aδ²) ≤ 2ρ < δ².
 – 2δ²ρ̂ = τ̃ + 2δ²S ≤ τ̂, since 2δ² ≤ 1.
 – 4τ̂ = 2d + 4S ≤ ‖z − z'‖ for distinct z, z' ∈ Z.

8. (d) Grouping. Group the terms by r (Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to). By step 6, the sets U^{τ̃}_ρ(y) with r(y) = z are pairwise disjoint Borel sets; by step 7 they lie in U^{τ̂}_{ρ̂}(z). Hence
 Σ_{y∈s} μ(U^{τ̃}_ρ(y)) = Σ_{z∈Z} μ(⋃_{y∈s, r(y)=z} U^{τ̃}_ρ(y)) ≤ Σ_{z∈Z} μ(U^{τ̂}_{ρ̂}(z)).
 Divide by ρ^n and write 1/ρ^n = (ρ̂/ρ)^n/ρ̂^n, where (ρ̂/ρ)^n ≤ (1 + aδ²)^n ≤ 1 + bδ² by (F1) with u = aδ² ≤ 1:
 Σ_{y∈s} μ(U^{τ̃}_ρ(y))/ρ^n ≤ (1 + bδ²)·Σ_{z∈Z} μ(U^{τ̂}_{ρ̂}(z))/ρ̂^n.

9. (e) Induction hypothesis. Every z ∈ Z ⊆ s satisfies the per-point hypotheses. Also #Z ≤ k − 1 ≤ m, δ ≤ δ_{m+1} ≤ δ_m, 0 < ρ̂ ≤ δ², 2δ²ρ̂ ≤ τ̂, and 4τ̂ ≤ ‖z − z'‖ for distinct z, z' ∈ Z. So the claim for m with σ' := ρ̂ and τ' := τ̂ gives
 Σ_{z∈Z} μ(U^{τ̂}_{ρ̂}(z))/ρ̂^n ≤ (1 + c_mδ²)μ(B_1(x)) + c_mδ².

10. Combination. From steps 5, 8 and 9, and δ² ≤ 1:
 Σ_{y∈s} μ(U^τ_σ(y))/σ^n ≤ (1 + bδ²)[(1 + c_mδ²)μ(B_1(x)) + c_mδ²] + (m+1)Kδ²
  ≤ (1 + (b + c_m + b·c_m)δ²)μ(B_1(x)) + ((1 + b)c_m + (m+1)K)δ²
  ≤ (1 + c_{m+1}δ²)μ(B_1(x)) + c_{m+1}δ².
 This completes the induction. The statement holds with c := c_m and δm := δ_m. ∎
proof_key_steps: One point: (M_y) from σ ≤ δ² ≤ 1 − ε to 1 − ε, B_{1−ε}(y) ⊆ B_1(x), e^ε(1−ε)^{−n} ≤ 1 + 2^{n+2}δ²
Recursive constants c_{m+1} = max{2^{n+2}, b + c_m + bc_m, (1+b)c_m + (m+1)K}, δ_{m+1} = min{δ_m, 1/a}, a = 4(10(m+1))^{m+1}, b = (2^n−1)a
Induction step for #s ≥ 2: d = min distance < 2ε, ρ = d/(4δ²), τ̃ = d/2
(a) (C_y) with parameter d/4: each term ≤ μ(U^{τ̃}_ρ(y))/ρ^n + Kδ²
(b) the cylinders U^{τ̃}_ρ(y) are pairwise disjoint
(c) cluster_selection gives Z, S; enlarged cylinders U^{τ̂}_{ρ̂}(z), τ̂ = τ̃ + S, ρ̂ = ρ + S ≤ ρ(1 + aδ²)
(d) grouping by representatives: Σ_s ≤ (1 + bδ²)Σ_Z μ(U^{τ̂}_{ρ̂}(z))/ρ̂^n
(e) induction hypothesis on Z (#Z ≤ m) and recombination with c_{m+1}

0. Constants. Let C ≥ 0 be the constant of the sibling cylinder_monotonicity for (N, n), and K_C := C(1 + eΛ) ≥ 0. Let c ≥ 0 and δ_M > 0 be the constants of the sibling cylinder_cluster_bound for (N, n, K_C, M). Put A := 2 + 2c + 2c/ω + 2M·K_C/ω and δ' := min{δ_M, 1/2, 2^{−(n+2)}, 1/A} > 0.
